messages:
ops-bot: Pager triggered: GPU paging surge detected in us-west-2 (rtx-pool-3). Severity P2. 90th latency > 2s, 5xx rate elevated. Auto-annotate: possible kvcache growth + batch spike.

mike: ack — I'm taking first responder. standing up live triage in #eng-oncall if anyone needs real-time voice.

mike: quick telemetry snapshot:
```
metric: gpu_mem_used_bytes{pool=\"rtx-pool-3\"} avg=14.9GiB, p95=15.6GiB
metric: kv_cache_size_bytes{pool=\"rtx-pool-3\"} current=13.2GiB target=8GiB
metric: kv_frag_pct{pool=\"rtx-pool-3\"} went 12% -> 46% over last 30m
metric: batching_inflight{pool=\"rtx-pool-3\"} average_batch_size=30 -> spike to 48 in last 10m
errors: runtime OOM traces starting 12:07:33 UTC
```

raj: oncall handoff in 40m — update me on mitigation steps and customer impact and I can take next.

eva: customer-impact: support graphs show two customers with increased 5xxs (chat/completions endpoint). ~1.8% of total requests, some timeouts ~3s. Not yet escalated to S1 customers.

mike: sharing short log tail we pulled from node-12 (canary):
```
[12:07:33] ERROR runtime: CUDA out of memory when allocating 520MB
...
KVCache: current_size=13501427328 (12.57GiB) target_size=8589934592 (8GiB)
batcher: batch_size=48 -> allocate 48*context slots -> memory spike
nvidia-smi output:
GPU 0: 15816MiB / 16384MiB, processes: python(34521) python(34600)
```

carol: hypothesis 1: sudden workload shift (larger prompts or more concurrent chat) caused batching to grow and the KV cache not evicting fast enough -> fragmentation and OOM.

carol: hypothesis 2: recent rollout of kvcache tuning on 2026-03-10 reduced proactive eviction headroom (config: kv_eviction_threshold=0.85) which combined with larger batch windows causes sustained high mem and paging.

sara: mitigation idea: force a soft shrink of KV cache on rtx-pool-3 to regain headroom and temporarily cap batch_size to 16 while we observe. I can run config change if we agree.

mike: rolling canary change now: reducing max_batch_size 48 -> 16 on node-12 and node-14. Command: `rbctl patch pool rtx-pool-3 --set batch.max=16 --checkpoint now`

mike: also triggering kvcache soft-shrink: `rbops kvcache shrink --pool rtx-pool-3 --target 8GiB --dry-run=false`

ops-bot: Action taken by mike: batch cap applied to nodes [12,14]. kvcache shrink started (job id: shrink-4312345678).

mike: immediate post-change metrics: p95 latency down ~18%, gpu_mem_used avg down to 12.1GiB on canary. no new OOMs on canary in the last 6m.

eva: customer noise reduced but still seeing occasional 500s from older connections — support routing throttles applied. I'll keep channels updated.

raj: I'll pick up next. mike, please upload the full GPU mmap dump + dmesg and share link. Also add which container images were affected.

mike: uploaded artifacts: https://internal-artifacts/redwood/incident/4312345678/gpu-dump.tar.gz (contains nvidia-smi, pmap, dmesg, runtime logs).

carol: added metric queries and short timeline to the ticket: 12:03 first batch-size spike, 12:07 first OOM, 12:12 mitigation applied, 12:20 stable canary. Need to validate if any background process (checkpointing) overlapped with peak.

sara: RCA owner assignment: I'll lead post-incident analysis. Next steps: collect full set of pmap outputs across nodes, gather kernel OOM logs, pull request history for kvcache tuning around 2026-03-10, and reproduce with loadbench to confirm batch-growth + kvcache threshold interplay.

mike: quick note — we saw a rare allocation pattern: many small KV allocations causing fragmentation rather than contiguous free. pmap snapshots show free segments fragmented into lots of ~1-4MB holes. Could explain why 13GiB used still triggered OOM for a moderate new allocation.

ops-bot: Incident state changed: mitigation in place, monitoring. Please continue timeline building in thread.

raj: handoff: I'll be on for the next 2h; will iterate on hypothesis testing. If we see more OOMs after rolling caps are removed, we escalate to full rollback of the 3/10 kvcache change.

eva: customer comms: message queued for support to notify impacted customers we applied throttles and are mitigating; will send status in 30m if stable.

sara: logging checklist for RCA: add pmap for each impacted node, full redis/kvcache eviction logs, exact batch size distribution for last 1h, and per-request token histograms. I'll create a doc and link here.

mike: temporary mitigation summary for post-incident notes: 1) batch cap 48->16 on rtx-pool-3 (canary then global if stable), 2) triggered kvcache shrink to target 8GiB, 3) applied per-customer rate-limits for affected tenants.

ops-bot: Incident annotated: cause_hypotheses=[batch-growth, kvcache-eviction-regression, fragmentation], mitigations=[batch-cap, kvcache-shrink, tenant-throttles], owner=sara, severity=P2.

sara: I'll collect final timeline and draft RCA in 24h. Leaving this thread open for any late artifacts. Please drop any extra logs or queries here.

mike: pasted a couple of diagnostic commands we ran: `gdb --batch -ex \"set pagination 0\" -ex \"info proc mappings\" -p <pid>` and `python -m tracemalloc` for heap traces (when applicable).

carol: note to self: add a guard in the autoscaler that inhibits large batch windows when kv_frag_pct > 30%. Might avoid repeats.

ops-bot: Incident resolved -> status: mitigated. Marking last_update_ts=4312345899.

sara: thanks everyone — moving to post-incident RCA work and will ping when doc is ready. :thumbsup:
